correctness.rationale: Every cyclic XOR edge pattern corresponds to 2 actions exactly when parity is even; at each vertex C forbids two disagreements and R forbids two agreements. The trace plus signed trace is the parity projection. Tensorized trace products give moments by independence. The 4x4 matrices have the stated exact monic characteristic polynomials, and their eigenvalue power traces yield the formulas. Strict spectral inequalities prove exponential relative variance. A standalone standard-library checker independently enumerated action and edge solutions for 1016 type words up to length 9; exactly checked the moments for every type word up to 12; derived characteristic polynomials from Newton identities and compared the closed forms at 75-digit precision. Finite tests support but do not replace the arbitrary-length proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general exact annealed equilibrium count/second-moment theorem on arbitrary graph families would dominate the present formulas; no such theorem was established by inspected material. Generic PNE enumeration for each fixed type word can in principle compute a given finite case, but does not assert or immediately imply the explicit all-size annealed spectral identities without the new parity-tensor analysis. The older random-network statistical-mechanics text remains an explicit unresolved priority risk rather than being labelled noncovering.

value.rationale: The number of simultaneously stable assignments is a natural selection-multiplicity observable in heterogeneous network games, complementary to existence. The exact two-moment formulas identify a genuinely nonconcentrating annealed equilibrium landscape: exponentially vanishing probability of no pure equilibrium (known) coexists with exponentially growing coefficient of variation squared (new). This phase-sensitive result is not a textbook restatement of the known alternating obstruction, does not require a downstream theorem, and motivates further study of typical equilibrium counts and selection.
